subject_property.property_identifier: Gadi Sirampur and four villages (Nawadih, Koldih, Pandna, Chihutia)

issues_framed: Whether prior to the enactment of section 65-A of the Transfer of Property Act in 1929, a mortgagor in possession had the power to grant a permanent lease of the mortgaged property so as to bind the mortgagee.
Whether the permanent lease granted by the mortgagor was in the usual course of management.
rule_and_authority_applied: Transfer of Property Act (IV of 1882), ss. 66, 65-A
Madan Mohan Singh v. Raj Kishore Kumari (1916) 21 C.W.N. 88
Banee Prasad v. Beet Bhunjun Singh (1868) 10 W.R. 325
elements_analyzed: Authority of mortgagor as bailiff or agent of mortgagee
Conformability of lease terms to ordinary usage
proven_accepted_facts: Raja Nilkanth Narain Singh was the owner of Gadi Sirampur.
A simple mortgage was executed on 1st August 1914 in favour of Chota Nagpur Banking Association Limited.
Bank obtained a mortgage decree on 29th November 1921.
Bank purchased a third share of Gadi Sirampur in execution of decree on 28th October 1922.
Wazir Narain Singh granted a permanent lease of four villages on 5th November 1925 to Hiraman Ram.
Plaintiff purchased Gadi Sirampur at auction sale on 6th April 1935.
Defendants were in actual possession of the disputed villages.
Defendant 2 was sufficiently represented in the mortgage suit.
Plaintiff was subrogated to the position of the Bank.
rejected_contested_facts: That the grant of the permanent lease was a dealing with the mortgaged property in the usual course of management.
That the lease was valid and binding on the mortgagee/auction purchaser.
evidence_relied_upon: Prior Judgments and Decrees of High Court and Trial Court

defenses_accepted_rejected.defense: Lease was granted in usual course of management
defenses_accepted_rejected.reason: No allegation or proof was made that the grant was in the usual course of management; permanent lease is not conformable to ordinary usage.

defenses_accepted_rejected.defense: Lease did not impair security of mortgagee
defenses_accepted_rejected.reason: Even if security was not impaired, the lease was not in the usual course of management.

remedies_granted_denied.remedy: Restoration of Trial Court Decree in favour of Plaintiff
remedies_granted_denied.details: Appeal allowed; High Court decree set aside; Plaintiff entitled to khas possession.

winning_arguments: The mortgagor in possession has no power to grant a permanent lease unless it is in the usual course of management.
Section 66 of the Transfer of Property Act deals with waste, not the power to lease.
The burden of proof lies on the lessee to establish the lease was in the usual course of management.
The defendants failed to establish that the permanent lease was in the usual course of management.
losing_arguments: The argument that the lease was valid because it did not impair the security of the mortgagee.
The argument that the mortgagor had power to lease based on Section 66 or general ownership rights.
The contention that the auction sale could not end the lease.
missing_insufficient_proof: Proof that the permanent lease was granted in the usual course of management.
Proof that the lease terms were conformable to ordinary usage for agricultural land.
final_outcome: Appeal allowed. Decree passed by High Court dismissing plaintiff's suit set aside. Decree passed by trial court in favour of plaintiff restored with costs throughout. Plaintiff entitled to khas possession of the four villages.
